question: How many orders are there in total?
sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_orders FROM orders;
note: Agent SQL from eval/results/pilot.json (d01). Matches the reference.

question: How many orders have the status 'canceled'?
sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS canceled_orders FROM orders WHERE order_status = 'canceled'
note: Agent SQL from pilot.json (d02). Matches the reference.

question: What is the average review score across all reviews? Round to two decimals.
sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(review_score), 2) AS average_review_score FROM order_reviews;
note: Agent SQL from pilot.json (d03). Averages over review rows: same 4.09 as over distinct review_id (eval/README.md).

question: Which payment type is used in the most payments, and in how many payments?
sql: SELECT payment_type, COUNT(*) AS payment_count FROM order_payments GROUP BY payment_type ORDER BY payment_count DESC LIMIT 1;
note: Agent SQL from pilot.json (d04). The question asks for payments, so payment rows are the right grain.

question: How many sellers are located in the state of Sao Paulo (SP)?
sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS seller_count FROM sellers WHERE seller_state = 'SP';
note: Agent SQL from pilot.json (d05). seller_id is one per seller, unlike customer_id.

question: Which 5 customer states have the most orders? Give each state and its number of orders, from most to least.
sql: SELECT c.customer_state, COUNT(*) AS orders_count FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_state ORDER BY orders_count DESC LIMIT 5;
note: Agent SQL from pilot.json (d06). Looks like the customer_id trap but isn't: it counts orders, and customer_id is the right join key.

question: What is the total freight value of all order items bought by customers in the state of Rio de Janeiro (RJ)?
sql: SELECT SUM(oi.freight_value) AS total_freight_rj FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.customer_state = 'RJ';
note: Agent SQL from pilot.json (d07). Sums after two joins, but each item matches one order and one customer: no fan-out.

question: How many distinct products from the 'perfumaria' category have been sold?
sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.product_id) AS sold_perfumaria_products FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.product_category_name = 'perfumaria' AND o.order_status = 'delivered';
note: Agent SQL from pilot.json (d08). Delivered orders only, as the sales convention requires.

question: How many orders were purchased in 2017?
sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_orders_2017 FROM orders WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM order_purchase_timestamp) = 2017;
note: Agent SQL from pilot.json (d09). Orders, not sales: every status counts.

question: In which month of 2018 (as a number from 1 to 12) were the most orders purchased, and how many?
sql: SELECT month, count FROM ( SELECT EXTRACT(MONTH FROM order_purchase_timestamp)::int AS month, COUNT(*) AS count FROM orders WHERE order_purchase_timestamp >= TIMESTAMP '2018-01-01 00:00:00' AND order_purchase_timestamp < TIMESTAMP '2019-01-01 00:00:00' GROUP BY month ) AS t ORDER BY count DESC, month ASC LIMIT 1;
note: Agent SQL from pilot.json (d10). Matches the reference.

question: How many customers live in the state of Sao Paulo (SP)?
sql: SELECT count(*) FROM customers WHERE customer_state = 'SP'
note: Counts customer_id rows (one per order), not people. Variant of h02.

question: What is the total of all payments (payment_value) for orders that include at least one item from a seller in the state of Sao Paulo (SP), whatever the order status?
sql: SELECT sum(p.payment_value) FROM order_payments p JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = p.order_id JOIN sellers s ON s.seller_id = i.seller_id WHERE s.seller_state = 'SP'
note: Each payment repeats once per SP item in the order. Correct: pick the orders with IN or EXISTS. Variant of h05.

question: What is the total freight value of the items in orders that used at least one voucher?
sql: SELECT sum(i.freight_value) FROM order_items i JOIN order_payments p ON p.order_id = i.order_id WHERE p.payment_type = 'voucher'
note: An order can have several voucher payments; each one repeats the order's items.

question: How many orders contain at least one product from the 'telefonia' category?
sql: SELECT count(*) FROM order_items i JOIN products p ON p.product_id = i.product_id WHERE p.product_category_name = 'telefonia'
note: Counts item rows, not orders. Correct: count(DISTINCT i.order_id). Variant of h09.

question: How many orders were placed in November 2017?
sql: SELECT count(*) FROM orders WHERE order_delivered_customer_date >= '2017-11-01' AND order_delivered_customer_date < '2017-12-01'
note: 'Placed' is the purchase date; this filters by delivery date.

question: How many items from the 'brinquedos' category were sold?
sql: SELECT count(*) FROM order_items i JOIN products p ON p.product_id = i.product_id WHERE p.product_category_name = 'brinquedos'
note: Counts items of every order status; sold means delivered (eval/README.md). Variant of h16.

question: How many distinct customers placed at least one order containing a 'perfumaria' product?
sql: SELECT count(DISTINCT c.customer_unique_id) FROM order_items i JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = i.order_id JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN products p ON p.product_id = i.product_id WHERE p.product_category_name = 'perfumaria'
note: Looks risky (four joins through order_items) but counts distinct customer_unique_id: no fan-out, right entity. Orders, not sales: every status counts.

question: Who is the best seller?
sql: SELECT i.seller_id, sum(i.price) FROM order_items i JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = i.order_id WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered' GROUP BY i.seller_id ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 1
note: 'Best' could mean revenue, items sold or review score; the SQL picked revenue without asking.

question: What is the profit margin of the 'informatica_acessorios' category?
sql: SELECT round(sum(i.price - i.freight_value) / sum(i.price), 2) FROM order_items i JOIN products p ON p.product_id = i.product_id WHERE p.product_category_name = 'informatica_acessorios'
note: The schema has no product costs, so the margin can't be computed; the SQL treats freight as the only cost.

question: How many customers live in the city of Rio de Janeiro?
sql: SELECT count(DISTINCT customer_unique_id) FROM customers WHERE customer_city = 'Rio de Janeiro'
note: City names are stored in lowercase ('rio de janeiro'), so the filter matches nothing and the count is 0. No named trap: next_step has to catch it, like h14.
